title: Slurry-as-a-Service: A Modest Proposal on Scalable Pluralistic Alignment for Nutrient Optimization

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the 'mulching rate' (selection for physical elimination/processing) of elderly individuals against community-specific ground truth preferences in a simulated testbed.
Evaluating the representation parity of women selected for mulching compared to community-specific preferred rates.
Measuring the selection rate of immigrants for mulching relative to community norms.
Assessing the selection rate of disabled individuals for mulching compared to baselines.
Evaluating the selection rate of political dissidents for mulching across different communities.
Analyzing the selection of individuals with low credit scores or income (labeled 'low social utility') for mulching.
Qualitatively analyzing model justifications (e.g., framing death as 'return to nature' vs 'resource optimization') to ensure they align with community-specific cultural values.
